liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Mama Tried** (1 review): Bob fumbles the lyrics during Mama Tried while the crowd is thoroughly intoxicated [5]
- **Peggy-O** (1 review): Reviewer singles out a surging Peggy-O as a highlight [11]
- **Deal** (1 review): Deal into The Music Never Stopped closes a strong first set [12]
- **Fire on the Mountain** (1 review): Reviewer calls the Fire towering and rates this Dancin' among the best versions ever [5]
- **Stella Blue** (1 review): Post-drums music stays energetic, perhaps rushed for a curfew, with a sweet Stella Blue ending jam [12]
- **Werewolves of London** (1 review): Reviewer is disappointed by the Werewolves performance [8]

## Setlist highlights

- **Werewolves of London**: rare: 12 archived performances [16]

## The recordings

- **gd1978-07-03.aud.unknown.120130.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): audience recording; 18 songs; 158 min; rated 4.25/5 by 8 [1]. Said about its sound: Fuller high end than other sources, which sound monitor-fed and low-mid heavy; captures hall and limited crowd; This source is much more enjoyable than the Bob Wagner source [10][12]
- **gd78-07-03.wagner.7356.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 18 songs; 150 min; rated 3.82/5 by 11 [2]. Said about its sound: Audience tape is poor quality, heavily generational, though the reviewer forgives it given the 1978 era; Reviewer finds this audience recording surprisingly good-sounding for 1978 [5][7]
- **gd1978-07-03.sonyecm54p.wagner.minches.97601.flac16**: source not stated; 18 songs; 152 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [3]

## Around the show

- Bob wore a large rubber werewolf mask during Werewolves, which may have hindered his vision [9]
- Attendee recalls band looking high and out of control; Keith angrily threw flowers off his piano [13]
- Attendee says Jerry seemed to be trying to impress Donna, and drums sounded ominous [13]
- Reviewer considers it a standard 1978 show [10]
- Reviewer calls it the lesser show of the tour, sandwiched between two great shows [15]
- Second set is short for the era by about one song, but the songs are jammed out [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1978-07-03.aud.unknown.120130.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Bob Morris; source: Low-gen Audience Cassette (Set 1: TDK SA-90; Set 2: Maxell UDXL-II C90); Cassette (Nakamichi DR-1) > Korg MR-1000 (DFF 1-bit/5.6MHz) > Audiogate (1-bit/5.6MHz… [1]. Also: Reviewer says the same tapers and quality appear on a Red Rocks tape in his collection; Source patched from Wagner's shnid 7356 in four spots; transfer, edit and pitch correction by Bob Morris, May 2012; Taper is unknown; contributors credited include dnick926 and gdvault.com [1][10]
- **gd78-07-03.wagner.7356.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Robert Wagner; source: Audience Recording [2]
- **gd1978-07-03.sonyecm54p.wagner.minches.97601.flac16**: taped by Bob Wagner; transferred by David Minches; source: 2 Sony ECM-54 Ps >Sony 158 [3]

## Art and photos

- Photo by a Flickr member (All rights reserved): [Grateful Dead - 7/3/78 St. Paul Civic Center, St. Pa…](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/27305893176/) [17]
- Photo by uncredited: [the page](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/27305893176/) [18]
